question_text: What mathematical condition must a cost function `C(i, j)` satisfy to enable Divide and Conquer Optimization in 2D dynamic programming of the form `dp[i][j] = min_{k < j} (dp[i-1][k] + C(k, j))`?

options.text: Monge property (Quadrangle Inequality): C(a, c) + C(b, d) <= C(a, d) + C(b, c) for a <= b <= c <= d
Commutativity and transitivity across all states
Linear separability in dual coordinate space

answer_explanation: The quadrangle inequality (Monge property) ensures that the optimal transition point `opt(i, j)` is monotonic with respect to `j`: `opt(i, j) <= opt(i, j+1)`. This reduces the complexity from O(K * N^2) to O(K * N log N).
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: The quadrangle inequality (Monge property) ensures that the optimal transition point `opt(i, j)` is monotonic with respect to `j`: `opt(i, j) <= opt(i, j+1)`. This reduces the complexity from O(K * N^2) to O(K * N log N).
